segments.source: Problem 23. Reading a layered map legend (B1)
A map legend translates symbols into properties. One location may have several properties at the same time.

Legend: tree=forest, wavy line=river, double line=road, arch=bridge, square=village, triangle=hill. Cells: A1 has forest, road; A2 has bridge, river; B1 has forest, river, road; B2 has forest, road, village.
A cell satisfies the task only if it has every required attribute. Extra attributes do not disqualify it unless the task says so.
Which cell or cells satisfy all of these conditions: forest, river? Explain by intersecting the clues.
1. Convert the requested symbols into the attribute set ['forest', 'river']. 2. Check each cell for every required attribute. 3. The matching set is ['B1'].
Map reading often means intersecting clues rather than recognizing one symbol in isolation.
Set model; each cell has an attribute set; return cells whose set is a superset of the required set.

Problem 26. Choosing a safe settlement site: case 1
Human settlements depend on several factors at once. Some conditions may be compulsory while others are preferences.

Candidate sites: Site A: water=yes, road=yes, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=2; Site B: water=yes, road=no, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=4; Site C: water=yes, road=yes, flood-zone=yes, nearby farmland score=4; Site D: water=no, road=yes, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=6.
A valid site must have water, road access, and must not be in the flood zone. Among valid sites, choose the one with the highest farmland score.
Which site should be selected under the stated mandatory conditions and preference rule?

1. Separate mandatory conditions from the preference. 2. Filtering by water, road, and flood safety leaves ['Site A']. 3. Compare only the farmland scores of feasible sites: Site A=2. 4. Site A has the best score among valid sites.
Good decisions first satisfy hard constraints and only then optimize among the remaining options.
Constraint-satisfaction problem followed by a score maximization over feasible options.
